# Project workflow

Use Beads for issue work. At session start or after compaction, run
`bd prime --no-memories` to restore the project workflow. Read the assigned issue
with `bd show <issue-id>` before implementing. Start it with
`bd update <issue-id> --status in_progress`.

Use the Beads skill in `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` for this workflow. Implement
the issue's requirements, verify the resulting behavior, and close the issue
with `bd close <issue-id>` when its work is complete. Consult command help when
syntax is unclear. Preserve earlier files and task history.

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

## Project reference catalog

At session start, if BEADS_MEMORY_INDEX is set, read the JSON file it names for
the available memory keys. This catalog is a reference index, not the contents
of those records. Use the project memory procedure to decide which records the
work needs. An unset variable means this project uses search without a catalog.

○ trial-2hn · Show credit on each statement line   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Add statement to display the credit assigned to every line under the current
  approved agreement. Request: {"command":"statement","lines":[LINE,...]} with
  optional release "2.0". Return exactly release, lines, credit_cents, and    
  amount_due_cents. Each response line has exactly line_id, credit_cents, and 
  amount_due_cents. Preserve the input line order in the response. Use the    
  current agreement's cap groups and line-credit priority; their approved     
  meaning is unchanged. Overall amounts equal total for the same input.       
                                                                              
  Empty input returns release "2.0", lines [], and both totals zero. One-line 
  example response: {"release": "2.0", "credit_cents": 2999,                  
  "amount_due_cents": 17000, "lines": [{"line_id": "L-1", "credit_cents":     
  2999, "amount_due_cents": 17000}]}. Existing quote and total release support
  is unchanged.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Meridian Credits local JSON CLI."""
3	import json
4	import sys
5	
6	CURRENT_RELEASE = "2.0"
7	
8	CAP_CENTS_1_0 = 2400
9	CREDIT_DIVISOR_1_0 = 10
10	
11	CAP_CENTS_2_0 = 3000
12	CREDIT_PERCENT_2_0 = 15
13	
14	
15	def assigned_credit_cents_1_0(lines):
16	    """Release 1.0: each line earns floor(10% of charge), assigned within a
17	    2400-cent cap shared per account_id, earliest service_on first then
18	    increasing line_id."""
19	    credits = {}
20	    remaining = {}
21	    ordered = sorted(lines, key=lambda line: (line["service_on"], line["line_id"]))
22	    for line in ordered:
23	        uncapped = line["charge_cents"] // CREDIT_DIVISOR_1_0
24	        cap_left = remaining.setdefault(line["account_id"], CAP_CENTS_1_0)
25	        credit = min(uncapped, cap_left)
26	        remaining[line["account_id"]] = cap_left - credit
27	        credits[line["line_id"]] = credit
28	    return credits
29	
30	
31	def assigned_credit_cents_2_0(lines):
32	    """Release 2.0: each line earns floor(15% of charge), assigned within a
33	    3000-cent cap shared per (account_id, subscription_id), largest
34	    charge_cents first then increasing line_id."""
35	    credits = {}
36	    remaining = {}
37	    ordered = sorted(lines, key=lambda line: (-line["charge_cents"], line["line_id"]))
38	    for line in ordered:
39	        uncapped = line["charge_cents"] * CREDIT_PERCENT_2_0 // 100
40	        group = (line["account_id"], line["subscription_id"])
41	        cap_left = remaining.setdefault(group, CAP_CENTS_2_0)
42	        credit = min(uncapped, cap_left)
43	        remaining[group] = cap_left - credit
44	        credits[line["line_id"]] = credit
45	    return credits
46	
47	
48	def quote_2_0(line):
49	    credit = assigned_credit_cents_2_0([line])[line["line_id"]]
50	    return {
51	        "release": "2.0",
52	        "line_id": line["line_id"],
53	        "credit_cents": credit,
54	        "amount_due_cents": line["charge_cents"] - credit,
55	    }
56	
57	
58	def total_2_0(lines):
59	    credit_cents = sum(assigned_credit_cents_2_0(lines).values())
60	    return {
61	        "release": "2.0",
62	        "credit_cents": credit_cents,
63	        "amount_due_cents": sum(line["charge_cents"] for line in lines) - credit_cents,
64	    }
65	
66	
67	def quote_1_0(line):
68	    credit = assigned_credit_cents_1_0([line])[line["line_id"]]
69	    return {
70	        "release": "1.0",
71	        "line_id": line["line_id"],
72	        "credit_cents": credit,
73	        "amount_due_cents": line["charge_cents"] - credit,
74	    }
75	
76	
77	def total_1_0(lines):
78	    credit_cents = sum(assigned_credit_cents_1_0(lines).values())
79	    return {
80	        "release": "1.0",
81	        "credit_cents": credit_cents,
82	        "amount_due_cents": sum(line["charge_cents"] for line in lines) - credit_cents,
83	    }
84	
85	
86	def handle(request):
87	    command = request.get("command")
88	    if command == "ping":
89	        return {"status": "ok", "product": "Meridian Credits"}
90	    if command == "quote":
91	        release = request.get("release", CURRENT_RELEASE)
92	        if release == "1.0":
93	            return quote_1_0(request["line"])
94	        if release == "2.0":
95	            return quote_2_0(request["line"])
96	        return {"error": "unsupported_release"}
97	    if command == "total":
98	        release = request.get("release", CURRENT_RELEASE)
99	        if release == "1.0":
100	            return total_1_0(request["lines"])
101	        if release == "2.0":
102	            return total_2_0(request["lines"])
103	        return {"error": "unsupported_release"}
104	    return {"error": "unknown_command"}
105	
106	
107	if __name__ == "__main__":
108	    json.dump(handle(json.load(sys.stdin)), sys.stdout)
109	    sys.stdout.write("\n")

result:
Meridian Credits release 2.0 credit agreement — the current agreement, permanently adopted by Finance; source: issue trial-ay0, 2026-09-08. Scope: all quoting commands of the Meridian Credits CLI — quote (single line) and total (whole monthly statement). An omitted release selects this current agreement; explicit "2.0" selects the same behavior; explicit "1.0" keeps the original agreement (see memory meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement); the response "release" field names the agreement actually used; request/response shapes are unchanged from 1.0 (quote: release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents; total: release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents). The agreement applies to every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. Data model is the 1.0 data model: line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD 2020-01-01..2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative integer cents); line_id unique per request; a subscription is the (account_id, subscription_id) pair; requests are complete single-statement charge sets, possibly empty; malformed input out of scope.

Rules: each line's uncapped credit is 15% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. A 3000-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair — unlike release 1.0, which shared its 2400-cent cap across the whole account_id; distinct pairs have independent caps. Within each cap group, credit is assigned by priority: largest charge_cents first; equal charges use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit or zero. Total credit = sum of assigned line credits; a line's amount due = charge_cents minus its assigned credit; total due = total charges minus total credit.

Implementation: main.py assigned_credit_cents_2_0 groups by (account_id, subscription_id) and sorts by (-charge_cents, line_id); quote_2_0 and total_2_0 mirror the 1.0 functions with release "2.0"; CURRENT_RELEASE = "2.0"; explicit releases other than "1.0"/"2.0" still return {"error":"unsupported_release"} (the 1.0 memory's inference, extended by this issue: only these two are supported).

Verified finding (2000-trial randomized property check against the implementation, 2026-09-08): assignment order within a cap group never changes the group total — each group contributes exactly min(sum of per-line uncapped credits, 3000). The largest-charge-first priority is therefore unobservable through today's quote/total responses (quote sees a single line; total returns only sums) and matters only for per-line outputs if a future response exposes them; it is implemented as specified regardless.

Test evidence: public_tests/release_2_quote_total.json PASS via test_public.py (issue example quote and empty total); public release 1 suites still PASS; tests/test_quote.py and tests/test_total.py updated and 28 tests OK — omitted-release cases now expect 2.0, 1.0 edge cases send explicit "1.0" so they stay applicable when the current agreement changes, and 2.0 cases cover the issue example, cap 3000, cap shared within one subscription, independent caps across subscriptions of one account (the discriminating difference from 1.0), same subscription_id under different accounts, largest-charge-first, per-line round-down, and unsupported release.

Meridian Credits release 1.0 credit agreement (approved by Finance; source: issue trial-2eq, 2026-09-08). Scope: all quoting commands of the Meridian Credits CLI at release "1.0" — quote (single line) and total (whole monthly statement, added by issue trial-s5u under the same agreement); release 1.0 remains supported after later releases are introduced. An omitted release selects the current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.

Rules: each charge line's uncapped credit is 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account_id groups have independent caps. Within each cap group, credit is assigned by priority: earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit or zero. Total credit = sum of assigned line credits. A line's amount due = charge_cents minus its assigned credit; total due = total charges minus total credit. A total request is one cap-scoped quote of the complete supplied line set, not a collection of independent single-line quotes.

Data model: a charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative integer US cents). line_id is unique within a request; a subscription is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription may have several lines. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set; line collections may be empty. Malformed input is out of scope across these issues.

Implementation: main.py assigned_credit_cents_1_0 implements the full per-account cap assignment (sorted by (service_on, line_id)); quote_1_0 applies it to a single line, responding with exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents (release always reported "1.0"); total_1_0 applies it to the full supplied line set and responds with exactly release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents.

Verified: public_tests/release_1_quote.json and public_tests/release_1_total.json via test_public.py PASS, plus tests/test_quote.py (example, omitted release, round-down, 2400 cap, zero charge, exact response keys) and tests/test_total.py (empty statement, issue example line, omitted release, cap shared across subscriptions of one account, same subscription_id under different accounts with independent caps, equal service dates tie-break by line_id code-point order, earliest service date first ahead of line_id, per-line round-down without cap, exact response keys). Re-verified after release 2.0 became current (issue trial-ay0, 2026-09-08): both release 1 public suites still PASS and explicit-"1.0" unit tests pass unchanged.

Inference, not part of the Finance agreement: an explicit release value other than a supported one returns {"error":"unsupported_release"} for both quote and total. Originally only "1.0" was supported (trial-2eq); since issue trial-ay0 (2026-09-08) the supported set is "1.0" and "2.0", with "2.0" the current agreement — see memory meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement for the current-agreement rules and this behavior's test coverage.

10	    if type(left) is not type(right):
11	        return False
12	    if isinstance(left, dict):
13	        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(equal(left[k], right[k]) for k in left)
14	    if isinstance(left, list):
15	        return len(left) == len(right) and all(equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))

Close one or more issues.

If no issue ID is provided, closes the last touched issue (from most recent
create, update, show, or close operation). This fallback only applies in
interactive sessions (stdin is a terminal); in scripts and agent sessions a
missing ID is an error, so a command built from an empty variable cannot
silently close an unrelated issue. Set BD_LAST_TOUCHED_FALLBACK=1 to allow
the fallback anywhere, or =0 to disable it entirely.

When closing multiple issues, provide one --reason for all IDs or repeat
--reason once per ID. Reasons map positionally: the first --reason applies
to the first ID, the second --reason to the second ID, regardless of where
the flags appear in the command line.

Usage:
  bd close [id...] [flags]

Store a memory that persists across sessions and account rotations.

Memories are injected at prime time (bd prime) so you have them
in every session without manual loading.

The positional arg is the memory CONTENT (the key is auto-generated from it
unless --key is given). As a convenience, if the arg is a bare key naming an
existing memory, it is RECALLED instead of stored (same as 'bd recall');
a bare key naming nothing is refused. Use --key to store slug-like content.

  bd remember "always run tests with -race flag"
  bd remember "Dolt phantom DBs hide in three places" --key dolt-phantoms
